text:
Samir: Hey all — launching the community-operators-toolbelt repo v0.1.0 now. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-operators-toolbelt/releases/tag/v0.1.0

Samir: TL;DR: collection of lightweight k8s operator templates, Helm charts, and CI workflows to help teams deploy Redwood Dedicated & Private adapters faster. Packaged under Apache-2.0. Maintainers wanted — see MAINTAINERS.md in the repo.

Priya: :tada: Congrats! Where's the release note? I'll copy into the community newsletter.

Samir: Release notes are linked in the release page (see link above) — summary includes quickstart, example overlays (kind/onprem), and an infra smoke-test.

Ben: Licensing q: Apache-2.0 + CLA requirement? Also does it include kustomize overlays for on-prem?

Samir: Yes Apache-2.0. We ask contributors to sign the CLA (CONTRIBUTING.md). There are kustomize overlays under ./overlays/onprem and an example values.yaml for on-prem installs.

Anya: I'll schedule a maintainer onboarding session next Wed 10am PT. @Priya can you add to calendar and post to #community-events?

Priya: Yup — I'll add it and include a short agenda: repo walkthrough, maintainer responsibilities, and first-issue triage. Also planning to showcase during Hacknight if maintainers are OK.

ci-bot: release-bot: Created GitHub release redwood-inference/community-operators-toolbelt v0.1.0 — 5 artifacts uploaded.

Ben: Quick heads-up — I'd like to add an automated smoke-test that deploys to kind and runs a sanity route check. Will send a PR today.

Samir: Love that. If anyone wants to be listed as an initial maintainer, reply here. We're also offering a small stipend for the first 3 maintainers (details in the repo under MAINTAINER_GRANTS.md).

Anya: I'm in for maintainership. :raised_hands:

Priya: Adding a note: outreach to CNCF sandbox could be an option down the road, but let's stabilize maintainers and docs first.

Samir: Solid plan. Next steps are in README (how to get started, how to run the CI smoke tests, and how to apply for a maintainer stipend). Thanks everyone — please RT to relevant community channels and tag potential early adopters. :rocket:
